body:
It's definitely easier to read the output with `NamedModulesPlugin`... could it be made the default when not using `minimize`? 😄 

It seems that module `0` is also treating the `wtf` name as an import of a default value, but no `export default` or `export { ... as default }` is in any of the files.
I'm actually using the new `angular-cli@webpack` release. So I don't have any control over the `webpack.config.js` file, unless I manually hack it.
I have created a git repo with a very simple project which shows the issue: https://github.com/meenie/webpack-import-barrel-bug

I think I am having the same issue.  I can `export * from './file'` just fine, but the LAST (or top before I actually import somewhere) index.ts I have to do `export { SomeComponent } from './file';`

So in my case I have a app/shared folder.

in app/shared/header, I have my header component.

in app/shared/header/index.ts, I have `export * from './header.component';`

in app/shared/index.ts, I have to do `export { HeaderComponent } from './header';` instead of export \* which worked fine in systemjs.

When I do that named export at the top level index.ts file, I can then use that somewhere else as `import { HeaderComponent } from './shared';`

Please let me know if this is the same issue.
@281330: Yes, that's the same issue.  Tree-Shaking is not working properly.

Thanks!! 
Kind of unrelated to the specific issue, but you said that u cannot change the webpack config since its what angular-cli team thinks is best.  But how easy would it be to set up absolute paths so we can just do `import { Something } from 'app/shared/some-folder/something';` ?
I would be against doing that in my project.  Makes moving stuff around quite hard.

@LunicLynx: That actually didn't fix it for me.  Try this scenario:

```
index.js
first.js
second.js
```

index.js:

```
export {test} from './first';
```

first.js:

```
export const test = 'hi';
```

second.js:

```
import {test} from './';

console.log(test); // undefined
```
(Crazy hypothesis but) could this be a regression caused by 3a6b649? It does change the behaviour of star imports, even though it's of imports of commonjs modules.
@Kovensky I tried reverting that commit and it did not fix it :(.

Related question: Does Webpack 2 features any kind of optimization for reexporting?

In the first example above, the `main.js` compiled code should call `__webpack_require__` with the index of `first/second/thing.js` module?

@sokra This is still an issue.  If you run my test repo (https://github.com/meenie/webpack-import-barrel-bug) you will notice that [sibling files that import each other's exports](https://github.com/meenie/webpack-import-barrel-bug/blob/78069173c18008470aea85fdf9c8da21c822d627/src/app/first/second/other_thing.js#L3) via the Import Barrel don't work.  Funnily enough, it will work if you do a `setTimeout(() => console.log('From other_thing.js:', thing), 0)`.

I'm using `^2.1.0-beta.21`.

issue.title: dialog imports and exports dialogconfig

repository.name: components
repository.description: Component infrastructure and Material Design components for Angular

issue.body:
I looks like dialog.ts both imports and then reexports MdDialogConfig and MdDialogRef.  For me this is causing an error when I try to build with webpack 2 due to it trying to re-add the module. The error is:

Uncaught TypeError: Cannot redefine property: MdDialogRef

 I'm pretty new to modules in typescript but it seems weird to me that a component would import and then export something
